subject: english
question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Manoj has a bigger / farmhouse of one hundred / hectares near the city.
solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. "Manoj has a bigger".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence contains an error in the phrase "**Manoj has a bigger**."
 
• The use of the word "**bigger**" is incorrect in this context because the comparison is not clear or complete.
 
• In English, when using comparatives like "**bigger**," it is necessary to specify what is being compared. For example, "**bigger than what?**"
 
• A correct revision would be "**Manoj has a large farmhouse of one hundred hectares near the city**" if no comparison is being made, or "**Manoj has a bigger farmhouse than his neighbor**" if a comparison is intended.

Correct sentence: *Manoj has a large farmhouse of one hundred hectares near the city.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparatives and Superlatives:**
 
 
• **Comparatives:** Used to compare two things. Structure: "**Adjective + -er**" or "**more + adjective**" (e.g., taller, more beautiful).
 
• **Superlatives:** Used to indicate the highest degree among three or more things. Structure: "**Adjective + -est**" or "**most + adjective**" (e.g., tallest, most beautiful).
 
 
 
• **Common Errors:** Always ensure that the comparison is clear and complete when using comparatives.
